spec.description: Subscribe to the level 2 (L2) order book -- individual price levels with aggregated order quantities at each level -- for one or more currency pairs, including a CRC32 checksum of the top 10 bids and asks for local book verification.

symbol.description: Currency pairs to subscribe to, e.g. `["BTC/USD", "MATIC/GBP"]`.

depth.description: The number of price levels, per side of the book, to be received.

channel.description: The channel this push belongs to.

type.description: Whether this push is the initial snapshot or an incremental update.

data.description: One entry per subscribed symbol touched by this push.

items.title: BookData
items.description: One symbol's book snapshot or incremental change.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `"BTC/USD"`.

bids.description: Bid price levels included in this push.

qty.description: The aggregated quantity at this level; `0` means the level should be removed.

asks.description: Ask price levels included in this push.

qty.description: The aggregated quantity at this level; `0` means the level should be removed.

checksum.description: CRC32 checksum of the top 10 bids and asks, for local book verification.

timestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp of this book snapshot or update.

notes: Deviation from the assignment brief: the brief suggested modeling `bids`/`asks` rows with `prefixItems` (positional tuples). Kraken's WS v2 wire format documents and demonstrates them as named `{price, qty}` objects, not positional arrays -- confirmed both by book.md's `ResponseField` listing and by the worked checksum example on https://docs.kraken.com/exchange/guides/websockets/book-checksum-v2 (`{"price": "45283.5", "qty": "0.10000000"}`). v2's own design goal, stated on the WebSocket introduction page, is explicitly to move away from v1's positional/variable-length fields in favor of named objects. `prefixItems` describes a fixed-length heterogeneous row; `bids`/`asks` are homogeneous, variable-length lists of a repeated two-field record, which is rule 3's non-case -- so each row is modeled as `items: {title: "BookLevel", ...}` (a normal array-of-object), not `prefixItems`. Rule 3 (bounded `prefixItems`) is not applicable to any of the 7 endpoints in this batch: ticker/trade/ohlc/book/status/instrument all use named-object rows throughout, per v2's stated design.
